<p class="person-bio">
I’m interested in the abiotic and biotic drivers of ecological stability. Specifically, I develop concepts and methods for assessing the role of response diversity in driving stability, and I use ecoacoustic data to quantify ecosystem dynamics, change, and stability in real-world ecosystems. In my spare time, I enjoy reading, going to the cinema, drinking matcha lattes, and being Kyoto's least-requested DJ.
</p>

<p class="person-keywords-jp">
生態系の安定性・応答の多様性・音響モニタリング
</p>

     ACOUSTIC DATA RESEARCH SPECIALIST
     ====================================================== -->

<div class="person-entry vacancy-entry">

<div class="person-details">

<div class="person-name-row">
  <h2 class="person-name">Acoustic Data Research Specialist</h2>
</div>

<div class="jp-person-name">非常勤研究員</div>

<p class="person-position">
<strong>Research Specialist</strong> | Kyoto University, Japan
</p>

<div class="vacancy-meta">

<strong>Project:</strong> JST FOREST — Elucidating the drivers of ecosystem resilience through acoustic analysis  
<strong>Host institution:</strong> Graduate School of Agriculture, Kyoto University, Japan  
<strong>Start date:</strong> 1 January 2027  
<strong>Compensation:</strong> 30 hrs/week, ¥1,800/hr + benefits  
<strong>Application deadline:</strong> 31 October 2026, 17:00 JST (may close earlier if a suitable candidate is found)

</div>

<p class="person-bio">
I am recruiting a research specialist to work with the large-scale acoustic datasets generated by our ecoacoustic monitoring projects. The role will focus on receiving, organising, storing, backing up and sharing research data, together with preprocessing acoustic recordings, calculating acoustic indices, and using machine-learning models for species identification.
</p>

<p class="person-bio">
Depending on experience and interests, the position may also involve training and improving machine-learning models, processing and analysing data in R or Python, and developing and automating analysis workflows. Applicants should be comfortable working with large research datasets and enthusiastic about learning new analytical tools and technologies.
</p>

<p class="person-bio">
Research communication in English is required. Japanese language ability is desirable but not required. Applicants should hold, or expect to obtain by appointment, a PhD, or have equivalent research experience and technical ability at approximately postgraduate level.
</p>

<p class="person-keywords-jp">
Ecoacoustics · Acoustic data · Machine learning · R / Python · Biodiversity monitoring
</p>

<p class="person-bio">
JST創発的研究支援事業「音響解析による生態系レジリエンス解明」を中心とする研究プロジェクトの事務支援を担当していただきます。主な業務は、データ整理等の補佐業務、研究費の執行・管理、物品・機器の購入、出張手続き、学内外の関係部署や共同研究者との連絡・調整などです。
</p>

<p class="person-bio">

</p>

<strong>Host institution:</strong> Linköping University, Sweden

<p class="person-bio">
We are recruiting a fully funded PhD student to apply ecoacoustics to the study of species interactions and response diversity. 
</p>

<p class="person-bio">
The position is part of the wider ReDiLEEP Doctoral Network, which brings together researchers across Europe and beyond to investigate how response diversity contributes to ecological resilience and stability.
</p>

<p class="person-bio">
<strong>Eligibility:</strong> EU mobility rules apply. Applicants are not eligible if they have resided or carried out their main activity in Sweden for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately before recruitment.
</p>
